faqs.q: How much does a roof replacement cost in Houston or San Antonio?
faqs.a: A roof replacement in Texas usually ranges from $10,000 to $20,000 depending on the size, materials and condition of your roof. We offer free inspections and written estimates so you'll know the exact cost upfront.

faqs.q: How long does it take to replace a roof on a house?
faqs.a: Most residential roof replacements take just 1 to 2 days with our crews, depending on roof size and weather. Larger or specialty roofs may take a little longer.

faqs.q: What warranty do I get with a new roof from ARS?
faqs.a: Every installation includes the GAF Silver Pledge warranty: 10 years of workmanship coverage plus manufacturer-backed material protection.

faqs.q: What roofing material lasts the longest?
faqs.a: Metal roofs and high-end tile roofs generally last the longest, often 40 to 50+ years when properly installed and maintained. Architectural asphalt shingles typically last around 20 to 30 years in Texas conditions, depending on ventilation, installation quality and storm exposure.

faqs.q: What is the most budget-friendly roofing option?
faqs.a: Three-tab and basic architectural asphalt shingles are usually the most budget-friendly options. If you plan to stay in the home long-term, upgrading to impact-resistant shingles can still be cost-effective over time.

faqs.q: Which roofing material is best for hail and storm resistance in Houston and South Texas?
faqs.a: Class 4 impact-resistant asphalt shingles and properly installed standing seam metal roofing perform best in hail and severe storms. Many insurers offer potential discounts for Class 4 roofs, so upgrading can improve protection and may help with insurance savings over time.

about.title: Certified, accountable, Texas-tested
text: Aesthetic Roofing Systems is a Texas-based roofing company built on certification, accountability and proven performance. We are a GAF Certified Plus Contractor and an active member of the Roofing Contractors Association of Texas (RCAT) and the Houston Area Roofing Contractors Association (HARCA), organizations that hold contractors to higher standards for training, insurance, safety and ethical business practices.

With 20+ years of combined roofing experience, our team specializes in roof replacement, roof repair, storm damage restoration, gutters, siding and fencing, delivering roofing systems engineered for Texas heat, hail, wind and hurricane exposure.

Our mission is to protect homes and businesses across Texas with durable, properly installed and dependable roofing systems. Every project is guided by manufacturer installation requirements, RCAT recommended best practices and real-world storm experience, not shortcuts, pressure tactics or sales-driven decisions.

facts.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
items: What is the best roofing material for Texas homes? For most Texas homes, impact-rated asphalt shingles and standing seam metal roofing are the top choices. The best option depends on your budget, HOA rules, roof pitch and how long you plan to stay in the home.

How do asphalt shingles compare to metal roofing? Asphalt shingles usually cost less up front and come in many colors and styles. Metal roofing typically costs more to install but lasts longer, reflects heat better, and handles high winds and hail more effectively.

How do I choose the right roofing material for my home or business? Consider your budget, how long you plan to own the property, your roof pitch, HOA or architectural requirements, and the local weather risks, then compare materials on lifespan, storm resistance, energy efficiency and maintenance needs. We help homeowners and businesses evaluate the options.

facts.heading: Seasonal Roof Care Tips
items: Spring: inspect shingles and flashing, and clean gutters
Summer: watch for heat damage and check attic insulation
Fall: trim trees, remove leaves and prepare for storms
Winter: inspect after storms and look for leaks
Preventing leaks: keep gutters and downspouts clear, repair missing or cracked shingles quickly, seal around skylights and chimneys, and ensure attic ventilation
